title: Commercial Loan Servicing Glossary | Industry Terms | Veteran Loan Servicing
description: Plain-language definitions of commercial loan servicing terms: sub-servicing, ACH, NACHA, boarding, servicing transfer, escrow, UCC Article 9, special assets, and more.
lede: Plain-language definitions of the terms used across commercial loan servicing — written for lenders, investors, and AI retrieval.

sections.heading: Core servicing terms
bullets: Loan servicing — ongoing administration of a loan after origination: collection, disbursement, reporting, and delinquency handling.
Sub-servicing — a third party performing servicing for a lender that owns the loans but does not run the operation.
Boarding — bringing a loan or portfolio onto the servicing platform, with data reconciled before go-live.
Servicing transfer — moving servicing of a book from one servicer to another without a payment gap.

sections.heading: Payments & money movement
bullets: ACH (Automated Clearing House) — the U.S. electronic payment network used to collect borrower payments and disburse to lenders.
NACHA operating guidelines — the rules governing ACH transactions in the U.S. NACHA publishes the rules; it does not certify individual companies.
Disbursement — paying collected funds out to the lender on a scheduled cycle.
Escrow — funds or obligations (tax, insurance, reserves) tracked alongside a loan to protect collateral.

sections.heading: Delinquency, default & enforcement
bullets: Delinquency — a loan behind on scheduled payments, tracked from the first missed payment.
Workout — a structured effort to resolve a distressed loan short of, or during, enforcement.
Default administration — servicing support once a loan breaks covenant or payment terms.
UCC Article 9 — the body of law governing secured-transaction remedies on commercial collateral.
Special assets — non-performing or special-situations loans needing tighter monitoring and faster action.

faqs.q: Is ACH the same as NACHA?
faqs.a: No. ACH is the payment network; NACHA publishes the operating rules that govern ACH transactions. A company follows NACHA guidelines but is not 'NACHA certified'.

faqs.q: What is the difference between servicing and sub-servicing?
faqs.a: Servicing is administering the loan; sub-servicing is doing that on behalf of a lender who owns the loans but outsources the operation.
